tiers.note: Model ids and prices are configuration. Unverified prices use a conservative placeholder so a budget check fails before money is spent.

tasks.note: In-process execution. Suitable for development; no persistence across restarts.

storage.note: Development filesystem storage: real writes, but not shared across replicas and not durable. Configure S3_BUCKET before production.

research.note: Offline provider: findings are derived from stored brand knowledge and open gaps are labelled rather than invented. Configure RESEARCH_HTTP_ENDPOINT for live market research.

strategy.note: Strategy generation is available and produces founder-approvable drafts. Nothing is published, sent, spent or applied to a live account.

required_information: The Flow Connector source: manifest.json (manifest_version, permissions, host_permissions, externally_connectable).
The background service worker's message contract: message types, request and response payloads, and the extension id used for onMessageExternal.
How an extension-initiated generation is authorised (session token, native messaging host, or user-visible confirmation).
Where generated files land: a download URL, a local path, or an object store the backend can read.
Job lifecycle semantics: accepted / queued / running / failed states, timeouts, cancellation support and rate limits.
Terms-of-service confirmation that programmatic generation via the extension is permitted for this account.
flow_connector.note: The Flow Connector source is absent from this repository, so its protocol is unknown and no adapter is active.

creative.note: Creative Studio produces briefs, mock generation jobs and stored assets. Mock assets are synthetic frames, not model-generated artwork. Automated QA never claims visual verification; a human must review every asset.

source_gate.reason: No upstream package is configured or present. The DeepX Flow Connector source archive is not supplied to this environment, so U1-U7 cannot be implemented here and no source may be copied into this repository.
authorization_requirements: an attestation stored outside the package
upstream project URL and exact release tag or commit
the package tree digest the reviewer reviewed
the licence name, evidence file and that file's SHA-256
reviewer identity, review timestamp and evidence reference

remediation_requirements.requirement: Remove the wildcard token broadcast and the page-accessible get_token / get_flow_context handlers; keep bearer material inside the extension's isolated world.
Replace api_post(url, body, token) with fixed allowlisted Flow endpoints; validate method, schema and destination before attaching authorization; reject encoded, redirected and alternate origins.
Speak flow.bridge.v1 to the companion instead of running a second unauthenticated bridge on 8792: authenticated HELLO, Host/Origin checks, size and timeout limits, no CORS.
Ship a restricted tool surface (status, generate_image, generate_video, check_video_status, export_asset) and remove eval_script, native_*, batch/rapid/autonomous tooling.
Replace http://*/* and https://*/* with the Flow/Labs origins actually used, and justify each remaining permission.
Remove the post-submit retry; create one request id before dispatch, report UNKNOWN_SUBMISSION on a lost response, and never resubmit.
Implement export_asset: return media bytes (bounded chunks) for a correlated job instead of a Chrome download id.

limitations: A measurement proves what is on disk, not what the browser has loaded.
A challenge binds a report to a session; it cannot make a compromised machine honest.

trust_semantics.artifact_integrity_verified: the HELLO's digest claim matches the release; a claim, never evidence about the installed files
trust_semantics.installed_artifact_measured: read from disk by the local companion process, never submitted by the extension
trust_semantics.provenance_trusted: session trust: measured locally, matched to a signed release, still inside its validity window

upstream_blockers.finding: content-script-main.js posts DEEPX_AUTH_TOKEN_CAPTURED with window.postMessage(..., '*') and answers get_token / get_flow_context from any page script.
upstream_blockers.required_change: Delete the token broadcast and the get_token / get_flow_context handlers; keep tokens inside the extension's isolated world.
upstream_blockers.blocked_because: The extension source is not supplied and its licence is unconfirmed.

upstream_blockers.finding: api_post(url, body, token) attaches the bearer token to a caller-supplied URL.
upstream_blockers.required_change: Replace it with fixed, allowlisted Google Flow endpoints and return only non-secret results.
upstream_blockers.blocked_because: Requires editing content-script-main.js inside the extension package.

upstream_blockers.finding: The service worker connects to ws://127.0.0.1:8792/ws and sends HELLO without any credential.
upstream_blockers.required_change: Send pairing_id/pairing_secret in the HELLO frame and refuse to run unpaired; support the flow.bridge.v1 envelope.
upstream_blockers.blocked_because: Unmodified extensions cannot authenticate, so they are refused.

upstream_blockers.finding: eval_script, batch_generate, rapid_batch_dispatch, autonomous_storyboard_pipeline, rename_project and open_new_project are registered MCP tools.
upstream_blockers.required_change: Ship a restricted build, or gate the powerful tools behind a local developer flag that Crusor never sets.
upstream_blockers.blocked_because: Tool registration lives in the third-party MCP server.

upstream_blockers.finding: manifest.json declares http://*/* and https://*/* host permissions.
upstream_blockers.required_change: Reduce to the Flow/Labs hosts actually used and document each one.
upstream_blockers.blocked_because: manifest.json is part of the third-party package.

upstream_blockers.finding: fastFillAndSubmitPrompt re-modifies the prompt and retries once when it cannot observe that submission succeeded.
upstream_blockers.required_change: After the submit action is dispatched, report UNKNOWN_SUBMISSION and stop; never resubmit automatically.

upstream_blockers.finding: deepx_download_media returns {downloadId, status} and never hands bytes to Crusor; generation returns URLs that a remote backend cannot fetch.
upstream_blockers.required_change: Implement export_asset: return the media bytes (or stream them to a companion-issued one-time URL) for a correlated job.
upstream_blockers.blocked_because: Requires a new command in the extension service worker.

flow.note: Phase 3C.1 hardens the bridge, the command surface, the token boundary and the asset-export contract. Live Flow generation stays disabled until the upstream extension changes are delivered and Phase 3C.2 is accepted.

publishing.note: No platform is publishable yet: platform application credentials and a token vault (TOKEN_VAULT_KEY) are both required. Approval and scheduling are fully implemented and no publish is ever simulated.

transports.reason: Meta Marketing API needs META_ADS_ACCESS_TOKEN and META_ADS_ACCOUNT_ID; POST /ads/transports reports this as unavailable until both exist.
Google Ads needs GOOGLE_ADS_ACCESS_TOKEN, GOOGLE_ADS_DEVELOPER_TOKEN and GOOGLE_ADS_LOGIN_CUSTOMER_ID (the customer id with billing). Without all three the transport reports unavailable.
LinkedIn Ads needs LINKEDIN_ADS_ACCESS_TOKEN and LINKEDIN_ADS_ACCOUNT_URN, plus an app approved for the Advertising API. Without them the transport is unavailable.

ads.note: Paid campaigns can be drafted by an agent, but every external mutation requires a single-use founder authorisation bound to the exact proposal hash. No ads transport is implemented in this build, so launches are refused and recorded rather than attempted.
